title: Bank accounts with inheritance
description:
Build a small hierarchy, one class per file (`Account.java`, `SavingsAccount.java`, `CheckingAccount.java`). Money is in whole cents (`long`).

```java
class Account                          // Account(String owner, long balance)
    String getOwner(), long getBalance()
    void deposit(long amount)          // IllegalArgumentException if amount <= 0
    boolean withdraw(long amount)      // false (and no change) if amount <= 0 or not allowed
    long available()                   // how much can be withdrawn now: the balance
    void monthEnd()                    // nothing for a plain account
    String toString()                  // "<Kind> <owner>: <balance in euros, 2 decimals>", Kind is the class's simple name

class SavingsAccount extends Account   // SavingsAccount(String owner, long balance, double yearlyRate)
    monthEnd(): adds interest of balance * yearlyRate / 12, rounded to the nearest cent

class CheckingAccount extends Account  // CheckingAccount(String owner, long balance, long overdraftLimit)
    available(): balance + overdraftLimit
    withdraw(...): allowed up to available(); every successful withdrawal also costs a fee of 25 cents
    monthEnd(): if the balance is negative, charges 2% of the overdrawn amount, rounded to the nearest cent
```

`withdraw` in `Account` should use `available()`, so that `CheckingAccount` only needs to override `available()` and add its fee. The fee may take the balance further below zero.
hints: Because `withdraw` in `Account` checks `amount > available()`, a subclass that overrides `available()` changes the rule without rewriting `withdraw`. That is polymorphism working inside your own class.
`getClass().getSimpleName()` gives the name of the object's actual class, so one `toString` in `Account` serves every subclass.
